llm.summary: This writing helper has reasonable article-writing features, but it also asks for under-scoped command, API-key, and file-processing capabilities that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Read, grep, glob, retrieval, and article output are proportionate for research writing; declared exec capability and generic credential/API setup are higher-impact than the stated purpose requires unless tightly scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package is a single markdown skill file with no executable installer, scripts, or install-time mutation observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad writing triggers and includes quick-start instructions to configure API keys, initialize API connections, process files, and execute commands, but does not define specific allowed APIs, command whitelist contents, file boundaries, or confirmation requirements.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, or destructive behavior were found, but the skill does request command execution capability and discusses API credentials and local file writes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core research-article workflow is coherent, including source gathering, outlining, drafting, citation checks, and outputting articles, but the artifact later expands into generic file processing, API integration, API credentials, and command execution without tying those powers clearly to article writing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use it only in a limited workspace, do not provide secrets unless a specific external source is genuinely needed, keep API keys in environment variables, and require explicit approval for any command execution or external API call.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: artifact lines around the main features add generic file handling and command execution beyond the article-crafting purpose, with no concrete limits.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the later quick-start explicitly tells users to configure API keys, initialize API connections, call APIs, process files, and execute commands, which is broader than the writing workflow disclosed at the top.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded as a standalone issue because broad writing-related triggers fit a writing skill, but they compound the concern when paired with exec and API-key instructions.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: there is a safety section, but it is generic and later in the document; it does not give prominent, concrete scoping for credentials, external calls, command execution, or file boundaries.
